findings.description: Round-4 fixed design D5 so sandboxed proxy variables are SRT-authored only and the backend never injects them (`design.md` D5), but the normative vendor-dispatch requirement still says the child environment SHALL include backend-composed `path/proxy variables` (`specs/vendor-dispatch/spec.md` Prepared-sandbox requirement). An implementer following the OpenSpec SHALL statement would reintroduce backend-authored HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY/NO_PROXY on the sandboxed child, which D5 and the earlier GHSA/proxy-bypass rationale forbid. Align the spec with D5: backend authors PATH/state/credential/`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` only; proxy variables are exclusively SRT-authored after the backend strips them from the environment passed to SRT.
findings.existing_code:
The child environment SHALL be built from a positive safe baseline plus backend-authored state,
path/proxy variables and exactly the selected lane credential; unrelated parent secrets SHALL not
be inherited.

findings.description: The OCR nested-launch classification is still mechanically inconsistent with the AST-guard exemption rule. D10 and task 4.4 register `ocr_adapter.py` as an explicitly inherited-sandbox nested vendor process that must keep launching the `ocr` binary (`skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/ocr_adapter.py` `subprocess.run`), while both also say process APIs in registered production surfaces are rejected except the shared backend and an exact `(file,function)` Git/coordinator control-plane allowlist. As written, `test_no_vendor_subprocess_bypass.py` either fails on the required OCR nested launch or must invent an exemption the task’s “exempting only …” clause forbids. Extend the allowlist/registry semantics so the inherited-sandbox OCR nested launcher is an explicit permitted `(file,function)` exception (or otherwise carve nested-inside-parent-SRT launches out of the bypass guard without dropping OCR from the registry).
findings.existing_code:
The AST guard rejects process APIs in registered production surfaces except
the shared backend and exact named Git/coordinator control-plane helpers.
`ocr_adapter.py` is registered as a nested vendor process whose parent Python command is launched
through the backend; tests prove the nested process inherits the applied SRT boundary rather than
granting it a second unsandboxed launch.
